sentences.zh: 伊斯梅所做的是，如你所说，他装了电铃，浴缸里有源源不断的热水。

sentences.en: It's a floating hotel.
sentences.zh: 这是一座漂浮的酒店。

sentences.en: And he has a series of ships.
sentences.zh: 他拥有一系列船只。

sentences.en: Oceanic is the first one.
sentences.zh: “海洋号”是第一艘。

sentences.en: Then Adriatic, Britannic.
sentences.zh: 然后是“亚得里亚号”、“不列颠号”。

sentences.en: You'll see how we're going to get to Titanic.
sentences.zh: 你会发现我们将如何走到“泰坦尼克号”。

sentences.en: Well, they all end in ick, don't they?
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们的结尾都是“ick”，对吧？

sentences.en: Coptic, Ionic, Doric.
sentences.zh: 科普特号、爱奥尼克号、多立克号。

sentences.en: Seasick.
sentences.zh: 晕船（Seasick）。

sentences.en: Well, no, not seasick, you see.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不，不是晕船，你看。

sentences.en: No, because you don't have seasick.
sentences.zh: 不，因为你不会晕船。

sentences.en: Yeah, as you say, it's a holiday.
sentences.zh: 对，正如你所说，这是一场假期。

sentences.en: It's a treat to go on a white star crossing.
sentences.zh: 坐白星号横渡大西洋是一种款待。

sentences.en: And so Ismay, as you say, I mean, he's kind of pulled himself up by his bootstraps.
sentences.zh: 所以伊斯梅，正如你所说，我的他是靠自己的力量白手起家的。

sentences.en: And he's very tough, very hard.
sentences.zh: 而且他非常强硬，非常严厉。

sentences.en: And in the 1870s, you know, there's a particular crisis that could have derailed the entire company.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪70年代，你知道，发生了一场几乎能让整家公司垮台的严重危机。

sentences.en: When in 1873, one of his steamships, the Atlantic, runs out of coal on the way to New York.
sentences.zh: 当时在1873年，他的其中一艘轮船“大西洋号”在去往纽约的途中耗尽了燃煤。

sentences.en: They divert calls to go to Halifax to pick up coal and they end up hitting a rock.
sentences.zh: 他们改道去哈利法克斯加煤，结果撞上了一块礁石。

sentences.en: And the lifeboats are swept away.
sentences.zh: 救生艇被冲走了。

sentences.en: 250 lives.
sentences.zh: 250条生命。

sentences.en: About a third of the people on board the ship are loSt.
sentences.zh: 船上大约三分之一的人遇难了。

sentences.en: And it creates an enormous scandal.
sentences.zh: 这引发了一场巨大的丑闻。

sentences.en: It could have completely derailed the company.
sentences.zh: 它本可能彻底毁掉这家公司。

sentences.en: It doesn't because Ismay is the kind of man who's not going to be diverted by a crisis like that.
sentences.zh: 但它没有，因为伊斯梅就是那种不会被这种危机转移注意力的人。

sentences.en: But Tom, that's a reminder, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，这真是一个提醒，对吧？

sentences.en: That it is a floating hotel.
sentences.zh: 提醒人们它是一座浮动酒店。

sentences.en: These are holidays for some people, not for lots.
sentences.zh: 对某些人来说这是度假，但对许多人来说不是。

sentences.en: Most people, arrogance.
sentences.zh: 对大多数人来说，这就是傲慢。

sentences.en: But still a hint of danger in the Atlantic crossing, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 但大西洋横渡中仍然带有一丝危险，对吧？

sentences.en: It's not entirely certain that your voyage will be trouble-free.
sentences.zh: 完全无法保证你的航程会一帆风顺。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But the great thing that White Star are able to do is to convince people, basically, that you can go on it.
sentences.zh: 但白星航运最厉害的地方在于，他们能让人基本上相信你可以乘坐它。

sentences.en: It will be like a hotel and all risk of danger has effectively gone.
sentences.zh: 它就像一家酒店，所有危险实际上都消失了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this is obviously a massive boom area of development because, essentially, you can build bigger and bigger ships and you can make them more and more luxurious.
sentences.zh: 显然这是一个蓬勃发展的巨大领域，因为从根本上讲，你可以建造越来越大的船只，让它们变得越来越豪华。

sentences.en: And this is why it's a really good business to be in.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这是一个非常好的行业。

sentences.en: And so Ismay, looking ahead to the future, he wants to establish a dynasty.
sentences.zh: 因此，伊斯梅在展望未来时，想要建立一个家族王朝。

sentences.en: He has three sons.
sentences.zh: 他有三个儿子。

sentences.en: Of these three sons, only one develops an interest in the sea.
sentences.zh: 在这三个儿子中，只有一个人对海洋产生了兴趣。

sentences.en: And this is his middle son, Bruce.
sentences.zh: 这就是他的二儿子布鲁斯。

sentences.en: And Bruce, on one level, is a classic example of what happens when British industrialists become very rich.
sentences.zh: 从某种层面上讲，布鲁斯是英国实业家变得极其富有后所发生事情的经典写照。

sentences.en: They send their children to private schools where, basically, the sons are taught to be ashamed of their parents for having the wrong accent.
sentences.zh: 他们把孩子送到私立学校，基本上在那里，儿子们会因为父母带有错误的口音而感到羞耻。

sentences.en: Which is what happens.
sentences.zh: 事实也确实如此。

sentences.en: But at the same time, you know, daddy is not interested, really, in the heirs and graces that his young son has been taught.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，你知道，父亲其实并不在乎他年幼的儿子被教导的那些门第和礼仪。

sentences.en: I mean, it's purely a marker of status that he can send him off to private school.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，把他送进私立学校纯粹是一种身份的象征。

sentences.en: What he really wants is a guy who is going to be effective at running the company.
sentences.zh: 他真正想要的是一个能有效管理公司的人。

sentences.en: And so that is what Bruce does.
sentences.zh: 这就是布鲁斯所做的事。

sentences.en: The other two sons go off and become members of the landed gentry.
sentences.zh: 另外两个儿子则去当了乡村绅士。

sentences.en: Bruce Ismay does stay true to the source of his family's wealth.
sentences.zh: 布鲁斯·伊斯梅确实忠于他家族财富的源泉。

sentences.en: So it's brilliantly summed up by Francis Wilson, who wrote a wonderful book called How to Survive the Tannic or The Sinking of J.
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯·威尔逊对这一点进行了精彩的总结，她写了一本名为《如何在大难中生存》或《J·布鲁斯·伊斯梅的沉没》的精彩书籍。

sentences.en: Bruce Ismay.
sentences.zh: 布鲁斯·伊斯梅。

sentences.en: She said, Thomas, so Thomas Ismay, the father, was a Victorian, Bruce, an Edwardian.
sentences.zh: 她说，托马斯，也就是父亲托马斯·伊斯梅是个维多利亚时代的人，而布鲁斯是个爱德华时代的人。

sentences.en: The father stood for entrepreneurial strength and imperial greatness, the son for decline.
sentences.zh: 父亲代表着企业家的力量和帝国的伟大，而儿子则代表着衰落。

sentences.en: And maybe with the kind of symbolic resonance that shadows the whole of this story.
sentences.zh: 也许这种象征意义笼罩了这个故事的始末。

sentences.en: Thomas Ismay dies one year before the death of Queen Victoria.
sentences.zh: 托马斯·伊斯梅在维多利亚女王逝世前一年去世。

sentences.en: It's not just a British event of note.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是一件值得关注的英国事件。

sentences.en: It has international resonance.
sentences.zh: 它具有国际影响力。

sentences.en: The Kaiser sends a telegram of condolence to Ismay's widow.
sentences.zh: 德皇向伊斯梅的遗孀发去了唁电。

sentences.en: All the flags in Liverpool are hung at half mast and Bruce Ismay takes over.
sentences.zh: 利物浦所有的旗帜都降半旗致哀，布鲁斯·伊斯梅接管了公司。

sentences.en: And the first thing he does, Dominic, is to sell the company to J.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，他做的第一件事就是把公司卖给J·皮尔庞特·摩根。

sentences.en: Pierpoint Morgan.
sentences.zh: 皮尔庞特·摩根。

sentences.en: So there's a real succession element to this, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 所以这里面确实有传承的成分，对吧？

sentences.en: You mentioned the Logan Roy comparison.
sentences.zh: 你提到了与《继承之战》的对比。

sentences.en: So for people who haven't seen the succession, it's a great, great TV series modeled on the Murdoch family.
sentences.zh: 对于没看过《继承之战》的人来说，这是一部非常棒的电视剧，以默多克家族为原型。

sentences.en: And in that series, there's this sort of ferocious Scottish self-made man played by Brian Cox and then his sort of feckless sons and daughter who are competing to replace him,
sentences.zh: 在那部剧中，有一个由布赖恩·考克斯饰演的凶猛的苏格兰白手起家的富豪，还有他那些争夺接班权的、不争气的儿女，

sentences.en: who are never going to be as good, never going to be as hungry because they've been reared amidst wealth.
sentences.zh: 他们永远不会像父辈那么优秀，永远不会像父辈那样充满渴望，因为他们是在财富中长大的。

sentences.en: That's the story that Bruce Ismay because he'd gone to Harrow, hadn't he?
sentences.zh: 这就是布鲁斯·伊斯梅的故事，因为他去过哈罗公学，不是吗？

sentences.en: He is going to travel on the Titanic.
sentences.zh: 他将乘坐泰坦尼克号出行。

sentences.en: He is a very tall man.
sentences.zh: 他个子很高。

sentences.en: He's very polished.
sentences.zh: 举止十分儒雅。

sentences.en: A droopy moustache.
sentences.zh: 留着下垂的胡子。

sentences.en: He's polite.
sentences.zh: 他很有礼貌。

sentences.en: He's the quintessence of a gentleman.
sentences.zh: 他简直是绅士的化身。

sentences.en: I mean, that's what Thomas Ismay wanted.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是托马斯·伊斯梅想要的。

sentences.en: Also, he is going to survive the Titanic.
sentences.zh: 此外，他将在泰坦尼克号海难中幸存。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this will make him notorious.
sentences.zh: 这会让他声名狼藉。

sentences.en: But just for now, Dominic, why does he want to sell the company?
sentences.zh: 但多米尼克，就目前而言，他为什么要卖掉公司？

sentences.en: Well, basically, because Morgan has deeper pockets than anyone in the world and is offering him an obscene amount of money for it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，基本上是因为摩根的财力比世界上任何人都雄厚，并为这家公司开出了一个令人咋舌的天价。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we talked about the foundation of IMM.
sentences.zh: 所以我们讨论了国际海运公司的成立。

sentences.en: Morgan basically pays him 10 times the value of White Star's earnings plus a premium of $7 million in cash.
sentences.zh: 摩根基本上付给他白星航运盈利价值10倍的资金，外加700万美元的现金溢价。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he ends up buying it for $35 million.
sentences.zh: 所以他最终以3500万美元买下了它。

sentences.en: Now, there's a bit of a fudge, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 现在，这里面有点权宜之计，对吧？

sentences.en: Because the ships will still have a British flag.
sentences.zh: 因为这些船仍将悬挂英国国旗。

sentences.en: They'll still have British crews.
sentences.zh: 它们仍将使用英国船员。

sentences.en: And Ismay, as part of the deal, will carry on running White Star within the IMM combine.
sentences.zh: 作为交易的一部分，伊斯梅将继续在国际海运公司联合体内运营白星航运。

sentences.en: So that's why he does it.
sentences.zh: 这就是他这样做的原因。

sentences.en: But it's very like kind of anxieties in Britain at the moment about tech companies kind of listing themselves on the New York Stock Exchange rather than in London.
sentences.zh: 但这很像目前英国对于科技公司选择在纽约证券交易所上市而不是在伦敦上市的焦虑情绪。

sentences.en: There's that kind of feeling that prestige companies, cutting edge companies are being taken over by the might of American capitalism.
sentences.zh: 有一种感觉，即声誉卓著的公司、前沿公司正在被美国资本主义的力量所吞并。

sentences.en: And an additional anxiety is that ships are needed to transport troops.
sentences.zh: 另一个令人担忧的问题是，需要船只来运送军队。

sentences.en: So Thomas Ismay had loaned his ships to the British government during the Burr War to transport troops.
sentences.zh: 因此，托马斯·伊斯梅在布尔战争期间曾将自己的船只借给英国政府用于运送军队。

sentences.en: And there's a real feeling of anxiety about what this might be.
sentences.zh: 人们对这可能会带来的影响感到真正焦虑。

sentences.en: And so the British government then lean in and they give Cunard a massive bung.
sentences.zh: 于是英国政府介入，给了冠达航运一大笔巨资。

sentences.en: So Cunard is the rival British company.
sentences.zh: 冠达航运是英国的竞争对手公司。

sentences.en: Effectively to compete with this would-be monopoly that Morgan is setting up.
sentences.zh: 实际上是为了与摩根正在建立的这个准垄断企业进行竞争。

sentences.en: And because Morgan cannot buy Cunard, it means that he doesn't actually establish a monopoly.
sentences.zh: 由于摩根无法收购冠达航运，这意味着他实际上并未建立起垄断地位。

sentences.en: And so therefore, he is embroiled in exactly the kind of competition that he didn't want to have.
sentences.zh: 因此，他被卷入了那种他极力想要避免的竞争之中。

sentences.en: Yes, because the whole point with all of these American capitalists at the beginning of the 1900s is, as you say,
sentences.zh: 是的，因为正如你所说，20世纪初所有这些美国资本家的核心目的，

sentences.en: to establish complete market dominance and then to basically fix the prices to suit themselves.
sentences.zh: 就是确立绝对的市场主导地位，然后基本上通过操纵价格来满足他们自己的利益。

sentences.en: He can't do this, partly because the British government is sponsoring Cunard as a competitor.
sentences.zh: 他做不到这一点，一部分是因为英国政府资助冠达航运作为竞争对手。

sentences.en: But also because, Tom, some other people have entered the story, the Germans, the Germans.
sentences.zh: 但另一个原因，汤姆，是其他人也进入了这个故事，德国人，德国人。

sentences.en: So the Germans have turned up and they have two big companies.
sentences.zh: 德国人登场了，他们拥有两家大公司。

sentences.en: One is called Hamburg America and the other is Norddeutsche Lloyd.
sentences.zh: 一家叫汉堡美洲航运，另一家叫北德意志劳埃德。

sentences.en: And of course, the story of the 1890s, 1900s is one of tremendous German growth in all kinds of areas, science, engineering and so on.
sentences.zh: 当然，1890年代和1900年代的故事是德国在科学、工程等各个领域取得惊人增长的历史。

sentences.en: Shipbuilding is one of these things.
sentences.zh: 造船业就是其中之一。

sentences.en: So that at this point, 1903, which is the first full year of the existence of IMM and the existence of White Star under Pierpont Morgan's banner,
sentences.zh: 因此，在1903年这个时间点，即国际海运公司成立的第一年，也是在皮尔庞特·摩根旗下白星航运运营的第一年，

sentences.en: the four fastest ships in the world are all German.
sentences.zh: 世界上最快的四艘船全都是德国造的。

sentences.en: And they all have these very Germanic patriotic names.
sentences.zh: 它们都有着非常具有德国爱国色彩的名字。

sentences.en: Imperator, Vaterland, Bismarck.
sentences.zh: “统帅号”、“祖国号”、“俾斯麦号”。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So White Star had always been the company that set the standard for luxury.
sentences.zh: 因此，白星航运一直以来都是树立奢华标准的标杆公司。

sentences.en: But Hamburg, America in 1903 have a ship called America that has been designed by the people who designed the Ritz-Carlton hotels in London.
sentences.zh: 但汉堡美洲航运在1903年拥有一艘名为“美国”号的船，该船由设计伦敦丽思卡尔顿酒店的人员所设计。

sentences.en: And they have Ritz-Carlton standards.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有丽思卡尔顿的标准。

sentences.en: And this is beyond anything that White Star have ever done.
sentences.zh: 这超越了白星航运以往做过的任何事情。

sentences.en: And now the British companies have to fight back.
sentences.zh: 现在英国公司必须奋起反击。

sentences.en: So first of all, Cunard built three very famous ships, the Mauritania, the Aquitania and the Lusitania.
sentences.zh: 首先，冠达航运建造了三艘非常著名的船，即“毛里塔尼亚”号、“阿奎塔尼亚”号和“路西塔尼亚”号。

sentences.en: Of course, there's a great war connection, two of which make their maiden voyages in 1907.
sentences.zh: 当然，这与一场大战有着紧密的联系，其中两艘于1907年完成了它们的处女航。

sentences.en: That, of course, then puts greater pressure on Morgan and his combine.
sentences.zh: 当然，这给摩根及其联合体带来了更大的压力。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Clinton Dawkins, who we mentioned, the guy who describes him as Titanic, I mean, he says, what threatens to swamp us is this monstrous indebtedness for shipbuilding.
sentences.zh: 正如我们提到的克林顿·道金斯，那个将泰坦尼克号形容为灾难的人，他说，威胁要将我们吞没的是造船业带来的这笔庞大债务。

sentences.en: And I don't feel satisfied that we're not putting more big ships into the Atlantic than it can bear.
sentences.zh: 而且我并不觉得我们在大西洋投入的大型船只没有超出其承受能力。

sentences.en: So there is massive overcapacity in the shipping, but they have no choice but to compete with Cunard and with the German firMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，航运业存在着巨大的产能过剩，但他们别无选择，只能与冠达航运和德国公司竞争。

sentences.en: And, of course, you know, the White Star reputation is for absolute luxury.
sentences.zh: 当然，你知道，白星航运的声誉就代表着绝对的奢华。

sentences.en: And so that basically is where the idea for the Titanic and its two sister ships comes from.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上就是泰坦尼克号及其两艘姐妹船构想的来源。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So Ismay gets together with a guy who we'll come to in a little bit called Lord Piri.
sentences.zh: 因此，伊斯梅与一个我们稍后会提到的人聚在了一起，他就是皮里勋爵。

sentences.en: Lord Piri is the head of the shipyards, Harland and Wolfe in BelfaSt.
sentences.zh: 皮里勋爵是贝尔法斯特哈兰与沃尔夫造船厂的负责人。

sentences.en: And Ismay says, listen, what we could do is we could just go bigger and better.
sentences.zh: 伊斯梅说，听着，我们可以做的是把规模做得更大更好。

sentences.en: I mean, just go bigger than Cunard, bigger than the Germans.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，比冠达更大，比德国人更大。

sentences.en: And again, let's think about three ships and they're going to call them the Olympic, the Britannic and the Titanic.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，让我们考虑三艘船，它们将被命名为奥林匹克号、不列颠号和泰坦尼克号。

sentences.en: And these three ships will allow us to recapture the momentum and the reputation which we need to justify our existence as part of the J.B.
sentences.zh: 这三艘船将使我们能够重新夺回动力和声誉，这是我们作为J·B·摩根商业帝国的一部分来证明自己存在的理由。

sentences.en: Morgan business empire that has been created.
sentences.zh: 而这实际上，汤姆，这就是泰坦尼克号的起源，1900年代的金融世界，英德之间的竞争，

sentences.zh: 哦对，是的。

sentences.en: In Belfast, in what was the Harlan and Wolfe shipyards.
sentences.zh: 在贝尔法斯特，建在曾经的哈兰德与沃尔夫造船厂原址上。

sentences.en: It's a wonderful museum.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极其精彩的博物馆。

sentences.en: They have a brilliant section on this.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个很棒的展区专门展示这个。

sentences.en: All the kind of the clamour and the noise, they evoke it very, very powerfully.
sentences.zh: 所有那种喧嚣与噪声，他们还原得非常非常震撼。

sentences.en: So just a few details that I garnished from that.
sentences.zh: 所以我就从那里收集了几个细节。

sentences.en: They boasted Belfast Rope Works, which was the largest rope maker in the world.
sentences.zh: 他们曾拥有贝尔法斯特制绳厂，这是世界上最大的制绳厂。

sentences.en: And they had Sirocco Works, which was the world's leading fan and ventilation manufacturer.
sentences.zh: 他们还有西罗柯工厂，是世界领先的风扇和通风设备制造商。

sentences.en: And both of these, of course, supplied lots of material to the Titanic.
sentences.zh: 当然，这两家公司都为泰坦尼克号提供了大量的材料。

sentences.en: Of course, yeah.
sentences.zh: 当然，是的。

sentences.en: So Sirocco Works supplied 75 fans to the Titanic.
sentences.zh: 所以西罗柯工厂为泰坦尼克号提供了75台风扇。

sentences.en: So I'm guessing that's another reason why it's such a centre of shipbuilding, is that basically all the kind of raw materials that you need to build a huge ship
sentences.zh: 所以我猜这也是它成为造船中心的原因之一，基本上建造巨轮所需的所有原材料

sentences.en: are, you know, they're not just in the shipyards, but scattered around in the companies that dominate the industry of BelfaSt.
sentences.zh: 不仅都在造船厂里，而且分散在主导贝尔法斯特工业的各大公司之中。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Belfast is more akin in many ways to a sort of northern or Midlands,
sentences.zh: 所以贝尔法斯特在很多方面更类似于英国北部或中部地区的

sentences.en: British industrial city than it is with Irish cities, you know,
sentences.zh: 工业城市，而不像爱尔兰南部的其他城市，你知道的，

sentences.en: Cork, Dublin, Limerick, and so on further south.
sentences.zh: 科克、都柏林、利默里克等等。

sentences.en: So actually, there's a wonderful quotation in Richard Davenport Hines' book from an Edwardian visitor who comes from the south of Ireland.
sentences.zh: 事实上，理查德·达文波特-海恩斯的书中引用了一位来自爱尔兰南部的爱德华时代访客的一段精彩引言。

sentences.en: And he goes to Belfast and he's really struck by how different it is.
sentences.zh: 他去了贝尔法斯特，被那里的巨大差异深深震撼了。

sentences.en: He says,
sentences.zh: 他说，

sentences.en: And out of the water, beyond the custom house, dimly seen through smoke and mist, rose some huge shapeless thing, which I found to be a shipbuilding yard,
sentences.zh: 在水面上，海关大楼之外，隐约透过烟雾与薄雾，升起某种巨大的、没有固定形状的东西，我发现那是一个造船厂，

sentences.en: wherein 10,000 men were hammering iron and steel into great ocean liners.
sentences.zh: 一万名工人正在那里把钢铁锤打成巨大的远洋巨轮。

sentences.en: The noise of wheels and hoofs and cranks and spindles and steam hammers filled my ears and made my head ache.
sentences.zh: 车轮声、马蹄声、曲柄声、主轴声以及蒸汽锤的声音充斥着我的双耳，让我头痛欲裂。

sentences.en: So that's the way that mid-Victorians talked about Birmingham or Manchester or something.
sentences.zh: 这就是维多利亚中期的人谈论伯明翰或曼彻斯特之类地方的方式。

sentences.en: And this is the way that people in Ireland talk about BelfaSt.
sentences.zh: 而这也是爱尔兰人谈论贝尔法斯特的方式。

sentences.en: It's this terrifying temple to industrial modernity.
sentences.zh: 这是一个令人敬畏的工业现代性神殿。

sentences.en: I guess one thing that Belfast has that most industrial cities, although not all, I mean, think Glasgow and Liverpool, but most industrial cities in Britain don't,
sentences.zh: 我想贝尔法斯特拥有而大多数工业城市（虽然并非全部，我是说想想格拉斯哥和利物浦，但英国大多数工业城市没有）所不具备的，

sentences.en: is a very, very sharp sectarian divide.
sentences.zh: 是一个非常非常尖锐的宗派分歧。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Paul Rouse gives in his thing, Belfast has a pub for every 300 people.
sentences.zh: 保罗·劳斯在他的文章中提到，贝尔法斯特每300人就有一家酒吧。

sentences.en: But of course, what pub you go to is determined by your religion in BelfaSt.
sentences.zh: 但当然，在贝尔法斯特，你去哪家酒吧是由你的宗教信仰决定的。

sentences.en: So Belfast had been founded, largely Scottish and English Presbyterians in the 1600s, 1603, I think it is.
sentences.zh: 所以贝尔法斯特最初是在17世纪60年代（大约1603年）由主要来自苏格兰和英格兰的长老会教徒建立的。

sentences.en: But over time, as has happened with so many industrial cities all over Europe, not just in Britain, but in the United States,
sentences.zh: 但随着时间推移，正如欧洲各地（不仅在英国，也在美国）许多工业城市发生的那样，

sentences.en: what has happened is it has absorbed migrants from the countryside who tend to be Catholic.
sentences.zh: 情况是它吸收了来自农村的移民，而这些移民往往是天主教徒。

sentences.en: So in other words, Irish Catholics.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，也就是爱尔兰天主教徒。

sentences.en: So by 1911, the sort of breakdown based on confessionalism is
sentences.zh: 所以到1911年，基于教派划分的人口构成大致是：

sentences.en: 34% of the people of Belfast are Presbyterians, 30% of them are Church of Ireland,
sentences.zh: 贝尔法斯特34%的人口是长老会教徒，30%是爱尔兰教会教徒，

sentences.en: 7% of them are Methodists, so those are the Protestants, and then you have the Catholics, which is 24%.
sentences.zh: 7%是卫理公会教徒，这些是新教徒，然后天主教徒占24%。

sentences.en: And there is absolutely no love lost between them.
sentences.zh: 他们之间可以说是水火不容。

sentences.en: Well, Dominic, you did mention the pubs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，多米尼克，你确实提到了酒吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The most beautiful Belfast pub, The Crown, which is opposite the Europa Hotel, which in the Troubles was always being bombed,
sentences.zh: 贝尔法斯特最美丽的酒吧“皇冠”，就在欧罗巴酒店对面，在北爱尔兰冲突期间这里总是遭到炸弹袭击，

sentences.en: and has kind of beautiful compartments that the ladies would sit in.
sentences.zh: 里面有女士们曾经坐过的那种漂亮的隔间。

sentences.en: You can still sit in them now.
sentences.zh: 你现在依然可以坐在里面。

sentences.en: And this reputedly was owned by a Protestant and a Catholic, and the Protestant husband said that we would call it The Crown, and the Catholic wife said,
sentences.zh: 据说这家酒吧曾由一个新教徒和一个天主教徒共同拥有，新教徒丈夫说我们应该叫它“皇冠”，天主教妻子则说，

sentences.en: all right, but we're going to put the image of The Crown on the doorway so that everyone will trample it as they walk in.
sentences.zh: 好吧，但我们要把皇冠的图案印在门廊上，这样每个人进门时都会践踏它。

sentences.en: You're right, you're right.
sentences.zh: 你说得对，你说得对。

sentences.en: I mean, that's what I was told when I was there.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我在那里的时候，别人就是这么跟我说的。

sentences.en: I don't know whether that's true, but it's a kind of nice example of how, you know,
sentences.zh: 我不知道这是否属实，但这算是一个挺好的例子，说明了，你知道的，

sentences.en: maybe that's the way that you get both Protestants and Catholics into a pub.
sentences.zh: 也许这就是让新教徒和天主教徒一起走进酒吧的方式。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, there's another visitor, 1907.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，还有另一个访客，1907年。

sentences.en: Belfast hums with industry and calls itself progressive, yet underlying all this commercialism, all this thrift, all this cult of the main chance, there is a cast iron bigotry,
sentences.zh: 贝尔法斯特处处洋溢着工业气息，自诩为不断进取，然而在这所有的商业化、所有的节俭、所有对发财机会的狂热背后，却隐藏着一种铁板一块的顽固偏执，

sentences.en: a cruel, corroding, unfathomable, ferocious sectarian rancor.
sentences.zh: 一种残酷、侵蚀性、深不可测、凶猛冷酷的宗派积怨。

sentences.en: And Dominic, that ferocious sectarian rancor, I mean, that is very evident in the Holland and Wolf shipyards, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，这种凶猛的宗派积怨，我是说，在哈兰与沃尔夫造船厂非常明显，对吧？

sentences.en: Because they are overwhelmingly Protestant, the people who work there.
sentences.zh: 因为在那里工作的人绝大多数都是新教徒。

sentences.en: After the Titanic had sailed, there was a story told in the House of Commons, an MP said he'd heard a story about a Catholic workman being stripped
sentences.zh: 泰坦尼克号起航后，下议院流传着这样一个故事：一位议员说他听说过一个天主教工人的遭遇，他被剥光了衣服，

sentences.en: and roasted over a furnace by Protestant workers in the shipyard until other Catholics with sledgehammers piled in to rescue him,
sentences.zh: 在造船厂的熔炉上被新教工人炙烤，直到其他天主教徒挥舞着大锤冲进来救他，

sentences.en: threatening to kind of smash these guys' skulls to pieces.
sentences.zh: 扬言要把这些家伙的头骨砸得粉碎。

sentences.en: And this story was contested, so some people said, oh, this is totally not true, this is invented.
sentences.zh: 这个故事受到了质疑，所以有些人说，哦，这完全不是真的，这是捏造的。

sentences.en: But the very fact that such stories were told tells you about the rancor, as it were.
sentences.zh: 但会流传这样的话题，这个事实本身就说明了那种积怨，可以说是根深蒂固。

sentences.en: So there are riots in Belfast in 1909.
sentences.zh: 所以贝尔法斯特在1909年爆发了骚乱。

sentences.en: There are more riots in 1911 and in 1912, as the sort of two communities turn on each other.
sentences.zh: 1911年和1912年又爆发了更多的骚乱，当时这两个社群开始互相反目对抗。

sentences.en: Protestants, obviously, the overwhelming majority, they hold the levers of power.
sentences.zh: 新教徒显而易见占绝大多数，他们掌握着权力的杠杆。

sentences.en: But the talk of home rule is simmering the whole time.
sentences.zh: 但是关于地方自治的讨论一直在暗中酝酿。

sentences.en: And they are terrified that they will be absorbed into a Catholic-dominated, you know, home rule Ireland, which is the absolute last thing they want.
sentences.zh: 他们感到惊恐万分，害怕自己被吞并到一个由天主教主导的、你知道的、实行地方自治的爱尔兰，这是他们绝对最不想看到的事情。

sentences.en: And so all the time, without sort of going back to some of our favourite
sentences.zh: 所以一直以来，不用回到我们最喜欢的

sentences.zh: 《历史的余烬》那些比喻，局势正在升温，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yes, the lava is bubbling.
sentences.zh: 是的，岩浆在翻滚。

sentences.en: It is indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Waiting to erupt.
sentences.zh: 正等待着喷发。

sentences.en: I mean, the shipyards do seem to have been places where casual violence was kind of expected.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，造船厂似乎确实是一个普遍充斥着暴力的地方。

sentences.en: Because another intriguing detail that I learnt from visiting the museum was that the foreman would wear bowler hats, partly as a symbol of status,
sentences.zh: 因为我从参观博物馆中了解到的另一个有趣的细节是，工头会戴着圆顶硬礼帽，部分是为了地位的象征，

sentences.en: but also they would be kind of lead-lined.
sentences.zh: 但同时它们里面也是铅衬的。

sentences.en: Like Old Job's hat.
sentences.zh: 就像老乔布的帽子那样。

sentences.en: Yeah, in case, you know, a riveter would drop something on their heads.
sentences.zh: 对，以防万一，你知道的，有铆工会把什么东西砸到他们头上。

sentences.en: So there were clearly class tensions as well as sectarian tensions.
sentences.zh: 所以除了宗派紧张局势外，显然还存在阶级紧张局势。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: But I guess, you know, the bowler hat also, I mean, it's the symbol of the Orange Order, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但我想，你知道的，圆顶硬礼帽也是奥兰治勋章的象征，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's a kind of visual signifier of that.
sentences.zh: 它是那种视觉上的标志。

sentences.en: So again, the kind of class and religion is, I mean, it seems to have been a very potent factor in the shipyards that are building the Titanic.
sentences.zh: 所以同样地，阶级和宗教，我的意思是，在建造泰坦尼克号的造船厂里，这似乎是一个非常强大的因素。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The Orange Order, which commemorates the victory of William of Orange over James II in 1690, the triumph of Protestantism over Catholicism.
sentences.zh: 奥兰治勋章旨在纪念1690年威廉三世在博因河战役中击败詹姆斯二世，这是新教对天主教的胜利。

sentences.en: That is very strong in the Holland and Wolf shipyard.
sentences.zh: 这在哈兰与沃尔夫造船厂非常盛行。

sentences.en: So as you say, those of these foremen with their bowler hats will be prominent figures in the Orange Order.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，那些戴着圆顶硬礼帽的工头将是奥兰治勋章中的显赫人物。

sentences.en: Now, Lord Piri, interestingly, it's so interesting that he has set himself apart from that by backing Home Rule.
sentences.zh: 现在，皮里勋爵，有趣的是，他通过支持地方自治把自己同那些人区分开来，这太有意思了。

sentences.en: And of course, as the temperature does rise, his support for Home Rule becomes ever more controversial.
sentences.zh: 当然，随着局势不断升温，他对地方自治的支持变得越来越充满争议。

sentences.en: And he's shunned by Belfast Protestant establishment.
sentences.zh: 他被贝尔法斯特的新教当权派冷落。

sentences.en: They see him as a quizzling, as somebody who's jumped into bed with the illegitimate liberals over in London,
sentences.zh: 他们视他为一个叛徒，一个与伦敦那些非法的自由党人同流合污的家伙，

sentences.zh: 在他们看来，这些自由党人正试图把他们的国家拱手让给教皇。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.zh: 我们探讨了大西洋两岸的背景。

sentences.zh: 我们探讨了这座城市以及建造它的造船厂的具体背景。

sentences.en: And I think in our next episode, let's look at the Titanic itself.
sentences.zh: 我想在我们的下一期节目中，让我们来看看泰坦尼克号本身。

sentences.en: Let's look at why it gets the name it does, how it's built, the fittings, the crew, and we'll get it out onto the ocean.

sentences.en: Okay.

sentences.zh: 好极了。

sentences.zh: 我们下次再见。

sentences.zh: 现在，汤姆，《历史的余烬》的我们，最喜欢航行了，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 我觉得我们非常像史密斯船长和查尔斯·莱特勒。

sentences.zh: 我们在船上提供舱位，对吧？

sentences.zh: 所以，不要迟疑，前往那个网站，therestishistory.com，走出三等舱，我们
